name: Do I need a permit to replace exterior stucco, siding, or wall finish in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit to replace stucco, siding, or an exterior wall finish on my house in Los Angeles or nearby cities?
mainEntity.text: Do I need a permit to replace stucco, siding, or an exterior wall finish on my house in Los Angeles or nearby cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Exterior wall projects are one of the most confusing parts of a remodel because the permit requirement depends on what is actually being changed. If the work is only cosmetic, such as painting or a superficial finish refresh, it may not need a permit. If the project involves removing stucco, replacing siding, repairing damaged sheathing, changing wall assemblies, or altering structural elements, a permit is usually required in Los Angeles and often in surrounding cities as well. The biggest trigger is whether the work affects structure, weatherproofing, fire rating, or energy compliance. Homeowners should also check whether the property is in a hillside, historic, or multi-family zone, since those conditions can add review requirements. A contractor should confirm whether the scope is a repair, replacement, or alteration before work starts. If in doubt, ask for a permit plan before demolition begins, because unpermitted exterior shell work can create inspection delays, insurance problems, and resale issues later.
acceptedAnswer.description: In Los Angeles, exterior work that changes or repairs a building’s exterior shell often needs a permit, especially if it affects structure, moisture barriers, or fire resistance. Like-for-like cosmetic refinishing may be exempt, but full stucco replacement, siding changes, or wall repairs usually require plan review. The exact permit need depends on the scope and the city.
